original_question: Is there a Borel class of profinite groups whose isomorphism relation lies strictly between smooth equivalence relations and S∞-complete equivalence relations, in particular in the Abelian case?
target_in_paper: Section 6 (Andre Nies), under "Profinite groups," Problem 18, together with the immediately following update resolving the Abelian case.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s target problem: it asks for a Borel class of profinite groups whose isomorphism relation has intermediate complexity—strictly above smoothness and strictly below S∞-complete complexity—and it explicitly singles out the Abelian case.
missing_details: The comparison is specifically with respect to Borel reducibility.
The intended benchmark on the upper side is an S∞-complete isomorphism relation; the update phrases the lower upper bound concretely as being strictly below graph isomorphism.
To be stand-alone, the question should say that the objects form a Borel class in some standard Borel coding of profinite groups.
For profinite groups, the intended equivalence relation is topological group isomorphism, not merely an unspecified notion of abstract equivalence.
The Abelian subquestion should be stated as asking whether the class of profinite Abelian groups itself provides such an intermediate example.
The nearby update records that this Abelian subquestion was answered positively via Pontryagin duality with countable torsion Abelian groups; that paper-faithful context is missing from the draft.
refined_question: Does there exist a Borel class C of profinite groups such that, under Borel reducibility, the topological isomorphism relation on C is properly between smooth and S∞-complete? In particular, can one take C to be the class of profinite Abelian groups?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation. Problem 18 in Section 6 asks essentially exactly this question, and its second sentence explicitly isolates the Abelian case. The main improvements needed are only to make the descriptive-set-theoretic ordering explicit (Borel reducibility), to specify that the equivalence relation is isomorphism of profinite groups in the profinite/topological sense, and to indicate that the Abelian instance means the class of profinite Abelian groups. The update immediately after Problem 18 is also important context: it states that the Abelian case has a positive answer, using Pontryagin duality to identify profinite Abelian groups with countable torsion Abelian groups, whose isomorphism relation is Σ^1_1-complete, strictly above smooth, strictly below graph isomorphism, and not above E0.
